entries.description: Read project-guidance.md, lessons-learned.md (relevant sections), session-set-authoring-guide.md, ai-led-session-workflow.md UAT/E2E pipeline section, and spec.md.
Confirmed restore-devidp set is COMPLETE (change-log.md present).
Authored ai-assignment.md directly (per human override on routing for this session).

In sibling repo dabbler-uat-dsl: shipped FOLLOW LINK IN NEW TAB verb (grammar/AST/validator/emitter), active-page tracking via currentPage local in emitted code, anchored visible-text regex with whitespace tolerance + IgnoreCase for CLICK BUTTON/LINK/TAB/MENU ITEM, .mud-popover-open scoping for menu items / dropdown options, row locators via Filter(HasText) chains, EXPAND ROW chevron click, Click + Clear + PressSequentially for inputs (per-keystroke), VERIFY SNACKBAR HasText filter, Exact:true on all GetByLabel calls. All 199 unit tests passing.

Repo-local: PlaywrightFixture.WaitForQuietAsync layered probe (data-actions-in-flight -> data-blazor-ready -> no-op); PlaywrightFixtureUatAdapter un-stubbed; dabbler-tracked-actions.js MutationObserver auto-bootstrap (fires regardless of layout); ComponentCatalogCrawler records visible text + aria-label separately (visible text wins for non-icon controls); crawler follows target=_blank links via RunAndWaitForPopupAsync; CustomerDataProvider.FindSearchFilter reads CompositeFilter.Filters; ComplianceReviewTab adds <HierarchyColumn /> to surface row expander; security-config.json MaskExemptions cleaned to [].
Authored sensitive-field-masking-audit-uat-remediation-uat-checklist.json with 6 UATs against real catalog, visible-text labels, role-switch flows.

Human ran UAT manually: UAT-1, UAT-2, UAT-4, UAT-5, UAT-6 passed. UAT-3 ambiguous: SSN field rendered without mask but value was empty for james.smith@example.com, so the human could not confirm an exemption-delivered unmasked SSN.

Diagnosed UAT-3 empty-input. Two issues found: (1) Web role-switch state was not propagated to API, so the API evaluated permissions and mask exemptions against the user's natural admin claims rather than the active BackofficeUser role; (2) PermissionService.ApplyFieldPermissionsAsync did not consult MaskExemptions. Additionally, the actual Customers row for james.smith@example.com had SocialSecurityNumber=NULL in the DB despite SeedData.cs intending '123-45-6789' for customer 0 (the SSN column was added by an idempotent ALTER on a pre-existing DB, never backfilled).

Diagnosed UAT-3 'no value displayed' feedback. Initial hypothesis was a two-permission-systems mismatch (AppFieldPermission Hidden vs MaskExemption). Investigation showed AppFieldPermissions has zero rows for Customer.SocialSecurityNumber, so the API was never nulling it via PermissionService. The actual root cause was simpler: Customers.SocialSecurityNumber for James Smith (Id=1) was NULL in the dev DB. SeedData.GetCustomers sets '123-45-6789' for customer 0 only on initial seed; DatabaseInitializer.EnsureAcmeCoffeeSchemaAsync added the column via idempotent ALTER on a pre-existing DB, which doesn't replay seed data.

Codified the SSN backfill in DatabaseInitializer.EnsureAcmeCoffeeSchemaAsync: an idempotent UPDATE Customers SET SocialSecurityNumber='123-45-6789' WHERE Id=1 AND SocialSecurityNumber IS NULL, paired with the existing ALTER. Replay-safe (the IS NULL guard prevents resetting deliberately-cleared values). Verified empirically: NULLed the row in SQL, recreated api with --build, post-startup query returned '123-45-6789'.
Human re-ran UAT manually after backfill: all 6 UATs pass cleanly. UAT-3 confirmed showing the real unmasked SSN under active exemption.

Round 1 cross-provider verification routed via gpt-5-4. Verdict: ISSUES_FOUND ($0.0690). Two material issues drove follow-on work: (R1-1) the speculative X-App-Switched-Role propagation that had been added during diagnosis was trusted without API-side authorization (Critical security); (R1-2) the SSN backfill was applied manually rather than codified (Major reproducibility). Two other issues were verifier misreads (alleged lack of UAT pipeline evidence; alleged contradiction in masking behavior) and were clarified.

Attempted to address R1-1 by hardening the X-App-Switched-Role gate with a natural-roles + RoleSwitching.AllowedRoles intersection. Round 2 verification surfaced one residual concern about the AllowedRoles intersection (since fixed). Then post-fix W2 runs began intermittently failing on UAT-1's 'VERIFY TEXT contains XXX-XX-' assertion. Pass rate dropped from reliable to ~1/3.

Injected diagnostic console output (test-side page snapshot + binder-side resolution log + component-side render log) to find why the W2 was flaking 1/5. Initial finding: when failing, the customer detail page rendered an editable input element with the raw SSN value '123-45-6789'; body innerText didn't contain 'XXX-XX-' because <input>.value isn't part of innerText. Hypothesized RestrictedFormField initial-render race: Unrestricted default state → ChildContent renders before ResolveAsync replaces with masked span.

Fixed the initial-render race in RestrictedFormField: added _isResolved flag, gated the @if chain to render nothing until ResolveAsync sets the flag. Real defense-in-depth fix (closes a brief flash of the editable input on slow renders that humans on congested SignalR circuits could observe). 715 unit tests still pass including the 200 Dabbler.Security.Blazor tests.

Reverted the speculative role-switch propagation work in full: removed UserSessionContextConstants.SwitchedRoleHeaderName, the IRoleSwitcher header forwarding from UserIdentityHandler, the InternalUserMiddleware gate (incl. SecurityConfigurationManager method-injection), the PermissionService MaskExemption integration, and the API security-config.json RoleSwitching block. Rationale: with zero AppFieldPermission Hidden rows for Customer.SSN today, role-switch propagation does not change observable masking behavior. The Web's RestrictionBinder is the sole authority. The gate was speculative defense-in-depth for a scenario that doesn't exist in the current data shape, and it added attack-surface complexity without buying anything observable.

Continued instrumentation revealed the ACTUAL root cause of the W2 flake: NOT a render race in RestrictedFormField but DETERMINISTIC state pollution across runs. UAT-2 grants a MaskExemption that SecurityConfigurationManager persists to the container's writable /app/security-config.json. UAT-3 in the same run sees the exemption and passes. But UAT-1 in the NEXT W2 run still sees the exemption and fails (because UAT-1 expects no exemption). Pattern: 1/N pass rate where the first run is clean and subsequent runs see the prior run's writes. Verified via `docker exec ... grep MaskExemptions /app/security-config.json` showing the persisted exemption that doesn't appear in the source-tree file. The BATON had explicitly warned about this earlier in the session ('Always force-recreate before re-running'); the warning was not enforced by tooling, only by documentation, so the footgun fired multiple times.

Added --reset-app-state flag to ai-router/uat_runner/cli.py. When passed, the runner force-recreates the web + api docker compose containers via `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.app.yml up --force-recreate -d web api` before running the checklist. This eliminates state pollution across runs by reverting the container's writable layer to the image's baked-in state. Cost ~10s per run. Skips gracefully when the compose file isn't present (developer running services from `dotnet run`). Empirical verification: 5/5 W2 passes with --reset-app-state on consecutive runs (where without the flag, runs 2-5 fail deterministically).

With the state-pollution fix in place, ~1/3 W2 runs still fail with a different symptom: System.TimeoutException waiting for `Locator('.mud-popover-open').Last` in UAT-2's OPEN DROPDOWN step. This is a separate, pre-existing W0-emitter race when MudBlazor's MudSelect popover is the SECOND popover of a tab — its render-then-ready timing varies enough that the 30s wait sometimes lapses. Documented as scope for the existing follow-on session set `docs/session-sets/uat-dsl-verify-input-value/spec.md` (which I'll expand to cover the OPEN DROPDOWN emit pattern as well as the VERIFY INPUT verb).

Round 3 verifier raised a Major: --reset-app-state was opt-in, not enforced for the canonical Session 1 run path; future engineers running cli.py without the flag would still hit the state-pollution bug. Closed by upgrading the runner to read a top-level `RequiresAppStateReset` field from the checklist JSON. When set, the runner force-recreates containers BEFORE running the test even without the CLI flag. Added `RequiresAppStateReset: true` to this checklist. Empirical: 5 consecutive runs WITHOUT the CLI flag now auto-reset and pass (modulo one pre-existing OPEN DROPDOWN popover-timeout flake on run 2 that's scoped for the follow-on uat-dsl-verify-input-value session set). project-guidance.md updated to document the field as the canonical signal for state-mutating checklists.
